purpose: Prevent tall/emergent-tree bias from producing false zero Elder Tree candidate results in dry, alpine, or slow-growth forests.

controls.source: US Forest Service Rocky Mountain Research Station
controls.evidence: Very old Rocky Mountain bristlecone pine stand near treeline; old-growth bristlecone intermixed with Engelmann spruce and alpine meadow.
controls.verification_scope: site-level ecological ground truth, not individual-tree GPS verification

controls.site: San Francisco Peaks Research Natural Area
controls.source: US Forest Service Rocky Mountain Research Station
controls.evidence: High-elevation spruce-fir / bristlecone landscape; USFS species review identifies the oldest known Arizona Rocky Mountain bristlecones on the San Francisco Peaks.
controls.verification_scope: site-level ecological ground truth, not individual-tree GPS verification

rule: A zero candidate result at a documented old-tree calibration site is a pipeline/ranking failure until demonstrated otherwise.
